explanation: 4 independent papers (2022–2025) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'task-scope-limitation'. What large language models know and what people think they know
The proposed uncertainty estimation algorithm has limited usage in free-form generation tasks because identifying semantically important tokens in generated sequence parts is non-trivial.
The chosen tasks relied on multiple-choice and numerical estimation formats rather than naturalistic open-ended generative tasks like writing or coding.
The evaluation focuses on specific question types involving small numbers of response choices (multiple choice) and short open-ended answers.
Experiments are evaluated primarily on classification and multiple-choice tasks with predefined candidate label sets rather than free-form text generation.

consumer.headline: 4 separate teams ran into the same wall: only tested on a narrow set of tasks
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: Several independent papers point at this, and we could read their full text to check.
consumer.why: 4 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 years. We could read 4 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.

caveats.label: Broadly worded
caveats.text: The problem these papers describe is worded broadly enough that they may not be running into quite the same thing.
